papers.title_in_file: A Model for Circuit Execution Runtime And Its Implications for Quantum Kernels At Practical Data Set Sizes
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results and Section V conclusions from plain pdftotext output; skimmed the appendix.
papers.what_it_is: An IBM Quantum paper that gives a heuristic runtime model for quantum kernel circuit jobs and checks it against Qiskit Runtime timings.

assertions.value: The authors report that their model predicts data sets of on the order of hundreds of feature vectors can be processed in order a few hours at current quantum computer speeds.
quotes: At current speeds of today's quantum computers, our model predicts data sets consisting of on the order of hundreds of feature vectors can be processed in order a few hours.
assertions.certainty_reason: Model prediction validated against runtime data from one service (Qiskit Runtime) in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: A model output, not a measured end-to-end run of a large data set.

assertions.value: The authors report that the model is most accurate when the job closely mimics those used to calculate CLOPS, and that it under-predicts runtime when the number of shots is small.
quotes: We validated the model's performance by comparing its predictions against empirical runtime information, and found the model is most accurate when the job closely mimics those used to calculate the CLOPS of a given system.

When the number of shots is small, the model consistently under-predicts runtime, due to the fact that, in reality, the software stack has fixed (and unavoidable!) overheads not accounted for by the model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison from one study on IBM systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum advantage with quantum kernels has yet to be attained in a practical context.
quotes: In a practical context, quantum advantage with quantum kernels has yet to be attained.
assertions.certainty_reason: A field-state statement in the introduction, with no single study behind it in this paper.

papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, parts of Section 5 experiments, and Section 6 conclusion; skimmed proofs.
papers.what_it_is: A mathematics paper that generalizes assignment flows from categorical distributions to density matrices on weighted graphs, with proofs and numerical illustrations.

assertions.value: The authors state the paper introduces assignment flows for density matrices as state spaces for representing and analyzing data associated with vertices of a weighted graph.
quotes: This paper introduces assignment flows for density matrices as state spaces for representing and analyzing data associated with vertices of an underlying weighted graph.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1: the paper defines the flow.

assertions.value: The authors state they regard the approach as a method for data representation and analysis, not a contribution to quantum mechanics.
quotes: We regard our approach merely as an approach to data representation and analysis, rather than a contribution
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1.1: the authors state their own scope.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical results indicate and illustrate the potential of the approach for data representation and analysis, including the representation of correlations of data across the graph by entanglement and tensorization.
quotes: Numerical results indicates and illustrate the potential of the novel approach for data representation and analysis, including the representation of correlations of data across the graph by entanglement and tensorization.
assertions.certainty_reason: Illustrative numerical experiments from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The experiments illustrate behavior; they are not a benchmark.

papers.title_in_file: Multiclass Portfolio Optimization via Variational Quantum Eigensolver with Dicke State Ansatz
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, ansatz description, and conclusion; skimmed supplementary material.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that uses parametrized Dicke states as a VQE ansatz for multiclass portfolio optimization with a diversification constraint, evaluated in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, combined with the CMA-ES optimizer, the Dicke state ansatz achieves superior performance in terms of convergence rate, approximation ratio, and measurement probability.
quotes: Our findings demonstrate that, when combined with the CMA-ES optimizer, the Dicke state ansatz achieves superior performance in terms of convergence rate, approximation ratio, and measurement probability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ansatz initializes the quantum system in a superposition of only feasible states, which inherently satisfies the constraints.
quotes: A key strength of this ansatz is that it initializes the quantum system in a superposition of only feasible states, inherently satisfying the constraints.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract: a property of the ansatz construction as the authors define it.

assertions.value: The authors state that all results were obtained through simulations, and that further investigation is needed to evaluate scalability and practical benefits in large-scale, real-world portfolio optimization.
quotes: All our results were obtained through simulations, as our primary objective was to gain a deeper understanding of the algorithm's potential for solving realistic portfolio optimization problems, encoding the diversification constraints in the quantum state preparation.
further investigation is needed to evaluate its scalability and practical benefits in large-scale, real-world portfolio optimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion, p.9: the authors state the limit of their own evidence.

papers.title_in_file: Toward Quantum Utility in Finance: A Robust Data-Driven Algorithm for Asset Clustering
papers.what_it_is: A short paper that applies the GCS-Q quantum annealing algorithm to clustering signed correlation graphs of financial assets, against SPONGE and k-Medoids.

assertions.value: The authors report that GCS-Q consistently achieves higher clustering quality than the classical baselines on synthetic and real-world financial data, as measured by Adjusted Rand Index and structural balance penalties.
quotes: Our experiments demonstrate that GCS-Q consistently achieves higher clustering quality, as measured by Adjusted Rand Index and structural balance penalties, while dynamically determining the number of clusters.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; the comparison is in figures.
assertions.reader_inference: Result rests on figures, not a table.

assertions.value: The authors claim that the work is the first, to their knowledge, to demonstrate a quantum advantage in solution quality using real hardware for the practical task of asset clustering.
quotes: This work is the first, to our knowledge, to demonstrate a quantum advantage in solution quality using real hardware for the practical task of asset clustering
assertions.certainty_reason: An author priority and advantage claim.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper lists benchmarking against Gurobi as a future step, so the comparison is not against an exact solver.

assertions.value: The authors report that GCS-Q is limited to roughly 175 nodes due to qubit constraints and hardware topology, and that clustering assets took over 10 minutes on average in practice.
quotes: Although GCS-Q is limited to roughly 175 nodes due to qubit constraints and hardware topology
In practice, clustering n = 170 assets with k = 10 took over 10 minutes on average, despite per-QUBO solve times being capped at 1 second.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured limit from one study on one annealer.

papers.title_in_file: On the Study of Partial Qubit Hamiltonian for Efficient Molecular Simulation Using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results, conclusion and future directions.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that truncates the qubit Hamiltonian to fewer Pauli strings for VQE molecular simulation and tests it in ideal and noisy simulators.

assertions.value: The authors report that a partial Hamiltonian is constructed with fewer Pauli strings that can resolve the entire Hamiltonian, so molecules can be simulated at a much lower computational cost with a truncated Hamiltonian.
quotes: a partial Hamiltonian is constructed with fewer Pauli strings that can resolve the entire Hamiltonian.
With PHA, we can simulate molecules at a much lower computational cost with a truncated Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results on small molecules from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the outcomes of the measurements with PHA quench the error due to noise introduced by the quantum circuits, and that the spread of simulation results is smaller for the partial Hamiltonian than for the full Hamiltonian.
quotes: the outcomes of the measurements with PHA quench the error due to noise introduced by the quantum circuits.
the overall spread of the simulation results appears to be smaller for partial Hamiltonian than the full Hamiltonian and the number of outliers is also smaller
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated noise models in one study, not hardware runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the performance of the method with larger and more complicated systems needs to be studied.
quotes: the performance of the method with larger and more complicated systems needs to be studied.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VIII: the authors state the limit of their evidence.

papers.title_in_file: Modeling Feature Maps for Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results on noise models, and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of how six quantum noise models affect QSVC, PegQSVC, QNN and VQC with three feature maps on a genomic sequence classification task.

assertions.value: The authors report that QSVC is notably robust under noise, whereas PegQSVC and QNN are more sensitive, particularly to depolarizing and amplitude-damping noise.
quotes: Results indicate that QSVC is notably robust under noise, whereas PegQSVC and QNN are more sensitive, particularly to depolarizing and amplitude-damping noise.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study on one genomic dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that the PauliFeatureMap is especially vulnerable to noise, and that testing accuracy decreases significantly with noise while training accuracy remains relatively stable.
quotes: The PauliFeatureMap is especially vulnerable, highlighting difficulties in maintaining accurate classification under noisy conditions.
The general trend observed indicates that while training accuracy remains relatively stable across varying noise levels, testing accuracy experiences a significant decrease.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state they apply the models to a genomic sequence dataset and assess noise by incorporating realistic noise models into their simulations.
quotes: In this work, we investigate the impact of quantum noise on various QML algorithms applied to a genomic sequence dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: Introduction: the authors state their own setup.

papers.title_in_file: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Feature Extraction approach for Image Classification using Autoencoders and Quantum SVMs
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results section A, channel-wise section and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A paper that feeds autoencoder-extracted features into simulated quantum SVMs for image classification on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and HTRU datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report that the autoencoder achieved near-perfect reconstruction and high classification accuracy for MNIST, while CIFAR-10 showed poorer performance due to image complexity and HTRU-1 struggled because of dataset imbalance.
quotes: The autoencoder achieved near-perfect reconstruction and high classification accuracy for MNIST, while CIFAR-10 showed poorer performance due to image complexity, and HTRU-1 struggled because of dataset imbalance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that running the pipeline through real hardware would be the main missing link, and that the expected results would be far worse on real quantum devices.
quotes: Running the pipeline through real hardware would be the main missing link, however, the expected results from this study would be far worse if they were to be run on real quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V: the authors state the limit of their evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that the autoencoder reduces images to 64 latent features per sample, which are amplitude encoded into 6 qubits for a QSVM and QOCSVM.
quotes: Using the autoencoder to encode the images into a reduced latent space of 64 features per sample, which is then amplitude encoded into 6 qubits for use in a QSVM and QOCSVM
assertions.certainty_reason: Section IV.A: the paper's statement of its own setup.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Spectral Clustering: Comparing Parameterized and Neuromorphic Quantum Kernels
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results (optimal k section) and conclusion.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing a parameterized quantum kernel with quantum neuromorphic QLIF kernels and an RBF kernel in spectral clustering.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the synthetic datasets and Iris the QLIF kernel typically achieves better classification and clustering performance than pQK, while on higher-dimensional datasets such as SDSS pQK performed better.
quotes: For the synthetic datasets and Iris, the QLIF kernel typically achieves better classification and clustering performance than pQK. However, on higher-dimensional datasets, such as a preprocessed version of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS), pQK performed better, indicating a possible advantage in higher-dimensional regimes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that running the full pipeline on quantum hardware is currently impossible because running a number of quantum circuit executions that are quadratically scaling is highly infeasible.
quotes: This is currently impossible because running a number of quantum circuit executions that are quadratically scaling is highly infeasible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V: the authors state a limit of their own method.

assertions.value: The authors state that the pQK could be improved by increasing the capacity or complexity of the quantum model.
quotes: The pQK could be improved by increasing the capacity or complexity of the quantum model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section V: the authors state a limit of the pQK as tested.
